rules.title: Hoboken rent increase cap at lease expiration or termination
rules.requirement: When your lease ends or renews (or for a periodic tenancy), your Hoboken landlord may not raise the rent by more than 5% or the CPI change, whichever is less. Only one such increase is allowed in any 12-month period, regardless of tenant turnover.
rules.key_value: lesser of 5% or CPI change; one increase per 12 months

coverage.summary: Housing spaces subject to Hoboken's Rent Control chapter (Chapter 155); this section does not itself state building-age or unit-count limits.

rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.

notes: Single section of Hoboken Code Chapter 155. The section was amended 2-1-2023 by Ord. No. B-532, but no effective date is stated, so effective_date is left null. Coverage exemptions such as building age or unit count are defined elsewhere in Chapter 155 and are not stated here.
